blocks.x: Care management succeeds on precision targeting and timely intervention: identifying rising-risk members, coordinating across providers, and proving quality outcomes. It is a data-discipline business — and the data discipline is usually the missing part.

The workflows we industrialize here: Risk stratification, Care outreach and scheduling, Program matching, Quality measure reporting, Provider coordination. Each arrives with its current cycle times measured in the Diagnose phase, and each leaves the program governed by outcome SLOs rather than anecdotes.

items: Claims, clinical, SDOH and engagement data siloed; risk stratification runs on claims only.
Care outreach, scheduling and follow-up run on call lists; gaps between contacts lose members.
Members matched to programs by blunt rules; engagement economics unmeasured.
Care teams share sensitive data across vendors; controls lag.
HEDIS-class measures assembled manually per cycle; evidence assembled under deadline.
Care platforms integrate by file export; workflows break at handoffs.

blocks.x: How we help — five priority capabilities

items: claims/clinical/SDOH unified with certified risk features — stratification precise
contact plans executed across channels with follow-up policy — completion up 25-40%
engagement likelihood + clinical need into assignment — economics measured
vendor access governed with monitoring — coordination secure
event-driven care workflows replacing file exports — handoffs reliable

blocks.x: We staff a named pod for this sub-industry pattern: delivery lead, quality owner and control owner, with the follow-the-sun rhythm covering build, run and the conformance monitoring that keeps the design honest after handover.

items: Clinicians get 90 minutes a day back — ambient documentation inside the EHR
